title: Assembly of fixed-object rectifications over sets
statement:
Let $\mathbf V=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ with its projective monoidal model structure [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model], let $W$ be its quasi-isomorphisms, and let $\mathcal D=\mathbf V[W^{-1}]_\infty$. Let $\operatorname{Cat}(\mathbf V)$ be all small strict enriched categories (a set of objects, mapping complexes, associative unital chain-map compositions) and enriched functors, allowing arbitrary functions on objects. For each set $S$, take the comparison $\eta_S$ of [lem-coef-fixed-object-enriched-rectification]. Let $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathcal D)_{\mathrm{Set}}$ be categorical algebras with discrete sets of objects: its fibre at $S$ is $\operatorname{Alg}_{\Delta_S^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal D)$, and its morphisms over $f:S\to T$ are algebra maps $A\to f^*B$. Let $\mathrm{FFB}$ be enriched functors bijective on objects and quasi-isomorphisms on every mapping complex. Then the coherently natural fixed-object comparisons assemble to an equivalence over the nerve of the category of sets
$$\eta:\operatorname{Cat}(\mathbf V)[\mathrm{FFB}^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathcal D)_{\mathrm{Set}}.$$
Its restriction to every fibre is $\eta_S$. On any dg functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ its object function is that of $F$, and its mapping-object maps, under the replacement comparisons, are the images in $\mathcal D$ of $\mathcal A(x,y)\to\mathcal B(Fx,Fy)$. The equivalence is one of infinity-categories, including the coherent naturality of these identifications. The strict total category also has a model structure whose weak equivalences are $\mathrm{FFB}$, whose fibrations are mappingwise projective fibrations, and in which every object is fibrant. Morphisms of its localized homotopy category can be represented by roofs $A\xleftarrow{\sim}QA\to B$, with $QA$ cofibrant and the backward map a trivial fibration. Thus every component of a mapping space in this localization is represented by such a roof.

source.place: Definition 5.3 and Theorem 5.4, obtained from fibrewise localization Corollary 4.22; specialize to Example 5.11. Read online, not archived. No Stacks tag gives this homotopy coherent fibrewise assembly. Remark 5.5 supplies the total model structure; the roof description is its cofibrant-to-fibrant homotopy-category computation. The roof and saturation computations use Hovey, Model Categories, Theorem 1.2.10(ii),(iv).

proof.text: By [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model], $\mathbf V=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ is left proper, tractable and closed symmetric monoidal and satisfies the monoid axiom. These are the hypotheses of Haugseng's Lemma 3.20, whose specialization [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model] supplies, for every small $S$, the combinatorial model category $M_S=\operatorname{Cat}_S(\mathbf V)$ with mappingwise weak equivalences (quasi-isomorphisms) and mappingwise fibrations (degreewise surjections). For $f:S\to T$ restriction takes $B$ to the category with homs $B(fx,fy)$; by [lem-coef-enriched-fixed-set-model] the restrictions form a strict contravariant diagram of complete and cocomplete categories, preserve all small limits and all weak equivalences, and have Quillen left adjoints $f_!$. The ordinary Cartesian total category of this diagram is exactly $\operatorname{Cat}(\mathbf V)$: a functor over $f$ is its family of maps $A(x,y)\to B(fx,fy)$ preserving units and composition, that is, a fixed-object functor $A\to f^*B$.

source.place: Lemma 3.20, Remark 5.5 and Example 5.11; identification of the Cartesian total category.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-grothendieck-fibre-localization] to $S\mapsto M_S$. Fix the universe of small sets and complexes first and then enlarge the ambient universes to contain its category of sets, every fibre and the total category; the smallness hypothesis of the cited theorem therefore holds. An arrow over $f:S\to T$ is in its total weak-equivalence class precisely when $f$ is bijective and the fixed-object map $A\to f^*B$ is a mappingwise quasi-isomorphism. This is precisely $\mathrm{FFB}$. Consequently $\operatorname{Cat}(\mathbf V)[\mathrm{FFB}^{-1}]_\infty$ is the Cartesian total infinity-category of $S\mapsto M_S[\mathrm{FF}_S^{-1}]_\infty$, and its fibre and transition functors are the indicated localizations.

source.place: Corollary 4.22, in its Cartesian opposite form, and Definition 5.3.

proof.text: The maps $\eta_S$ of [lem-coef-fixed-object-enriched-rectification] form a coherent natural equivalence under all restrictions $f^*$. Apply the natural-transformation assertion of [lem-coef-grothendieck-fibre-localization] to this diagram and the diagram $S\mapsto\operatorname{Alg}_{\Delta_S^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal D)$. Its second total category is exactly the categorical algebras with sets of objects in the statement, because arrows over $f$ are algebra maps into $f^*B$. The resulting total functor $\eta$ is an equivalence over the nerve of sets, and its fibre at $S$ is $\eta_S$. This applies to coherent natural transformations of infinity-categories and therefore proves an equivalence of infinity-categories, including all higher coherence, rather than only of their homotopy categories.

source.place: Theorem 5.4, using coherent fixed-object Proposition 5.2 and Corollary 4.22.

proof.text: For a dg functor $F:A\to B$ over $f$, use the factorization $A\to f^*B\to B$ in the ordinary total category. The Cartesian-localization comparison [lem-coef-grothendieck-fibre-localization] preserves this factorization and its base function. The fixed-object comparison [lem-coef-fixed-object-enriched-rectification] identifies the first factor on each mapping object with the localized chain map $A(x,y)\to B(fx,fy)$, using the natural equivalences from fixed-object cofibrant replacements. The second factor merely records $f$. This gives the claimed description on $F$; coherence of its identifications is the coherent restriction-naturality already included in that fixed-object comparison and the total comparison.

source.place: Definition 5.1, Theorem 5.4 and the Cartesian-arrow description in Corollary 4.22.

proof.text: Construct the total model structure explicitly from the fibre model structures of [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model] and the restriction adjunctions of [lem-coef-enriched-fixed-set-model]. For $F:A_S\to B_T$ over $f:S\to T$, denote its adjoint descriptions by $u:f_!A\to B$ and $v:A\to f^*B$. Declare $F$ a weak equivalence when $f$ is bijective and $v$ a fibre weak equivalence; a fibration when $v$ is a fibre fibration; and a cofibration when $u$ is a fibre cofibration. The total category has all small limits: take the limit $L$ of a diagram's object sets, restrict all its entries to $L$, and take their limit in $M_L$. Indeed a cone with object function into $L$ is exactly a fibre cone after restriction, and restriction preserves limits as a right adjoint. Dually, for a colimit object set $C$, extend each entry along its map to $C$ by the corresponding left adjoint and take their colimit in $M_C$. Adjunction identifies its maps into a target with compatible maps from the original diagram. These descriptions prove the total universal properties. Weak equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three: if two maps among $F,G,GF$ are weak equivalences, their base functions force all three base functions to be bijective, after which reindexing identifies the check with two-out-of-three in one fibre. They are retract closed, since bijections and mappingwise weak equivalences are retract closed.

source.place: Proposition 4.25, proof: limits, colimits, and two-out-of-three, specialized to sets.

proof.text: For a first factorization of $F$ over $f$, factor $u:f_!A\to B$ in the model category $M_T$ of [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model] as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration. Regard the first arrow as a total arrow over $f$ and the second as a total arrow over $1_T$. This factors $F$ as a total cofibration followed by a total trivial fibration. For the second factorization, factor $v:A\to f^*B$ in $M_S$ as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration, regarding the first arrow as over $1_S$ and the second as over $f$. This factors $F$ as a total trivial cofibration followed by a total fibration. Over a bijection, $f^*$ and $f_!$ are inverse reindexings, so the uses of the word trivial in these factorizations agree with the declared total weak equivalences.

source.place: Proposition 4.25, proof: the two factorizations; the second is written out rather than omitted by duality.

proof.text: In a total lifting square use base functions $f:S\to T$, $g:U\to V$, $a:S\to U$, $b:T\to V$ with $ga=bf$, and fibre arrows $v:A\to f^*B$, $w:X\to g^*Y$, $\alpha:A\to a^*X$, $\beta:B\to b^*Y$. Let $u:f_!A\to B$ be adjoint to $v$. The strict restriction diagram and its adjunctions are supplied by [lem-coef-enriched-fixed-set-model]. For any $h:T\to U$ with $hf=a$ and $gh=b$, apply [lem-coef-adjunction-square-lifts] to this diagram. It supplies a commuting square in $M_U$ with left map $h_!u$, right map $w$, and horizontal arrows the specified adjuncts of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Its diagonals are in bijection with total diagonals over $h$. This is the required square comparison, with both triangle equations included in the cited statement.

source.place: Proposition 4.25, proof: both lifting systems, with the omitted dual argument supplied; Remark 5.5.

proof.text: If the right map is a total trivial fibration, $g$ is bijective. Choose $h=g^{-1}b$; then $hf=a$ and $gh=b$. In the fibre square just constructed, $w$ is a trivial fibration and $h_!u$ is a cofibration because $u$ is one and $h_!$ is left Quillen by [lem-coef-enriched-fixed-set-model]. The fibre lifting axiom of [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model] gives a diagonal, and the bijection of [lem-coef-adjunction-square-lifts] gives the required total diagonal. If the left map is a total trivial cofibration, $f$ is bijective; choose $h=af^{-1}$, which again satisfies both equations. Bijection reindexing identifies $u$ with a fibre trivial cofibration. Now $h_!u$ is a trivial cofibration and $w$ is a fibration. The other fibre lifting axiom gives a diagonal, whose adjunct is the total lift over $h$.

source.place: Proposition 4.25, proof: both lifting systems, with the omitted dual argument supplied; Remark 5.5.

proof.text: Let $F:A_S\to B_T$ over $f$ have the left lifting property against every total trivial fibration (lifts need not be unique), and write its first factorization as $F=pi$ with $i:A_S\to Z_T$ and $p:Z_T\to B_T$ over $1_T$. The first clause of [lem-coef-factorization-lifting-retracts] supplies $d:B_T\to Z_T$ with $dF=i$ and $pd=1_B$. The latter equation forces $d$ to have base $1_T$. Taking adjuncts along $f_!\dashv f^*$ from [lem-coef-enriched-fixed-set-model] gives, in $M_T$, $d u_F=u_i$, $p u_i=u_F$ and $pd=1_B$. Thus $u_F$ is an arrow retract of the fibre cofibration $u_i$, with source components identities and target components $d,p$. It is a cofibration by the fibre retract axiom of [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model]. Together with step 8 this identifies total cofibrations with the left lifting class against total trivial fibrations.

source.place: Proposition 4.25, proof: both lifting systems, with the omitted dual argument supplied; Remark 5.5.

proof.text: If $F:A_S\to B_T$ over $f$ has the left lifting property against every total fibration, its second factorization $F=pi$ has $i:A_S\to Z_S$ over $1_S$ and $p:Z_S\to B_T$ over $f$. The first clause of [lem-coef-factorization-lifting-retracts] gives $d:B_T\to Z_S$ with $dF=i$ and $pd=1_B$. Its base $h$ satisfies $hf=1_S$ and $fh=1_T$, so $f$ is bijective. Write $d:B\to h^*Z$ in the fibre and put $e=f^*d:f^*B\to Z$ using $f^*h^*=1$. The two lift equations give $e v_F=i$ and $v_p e=1_{f^*B}$, while the factorization gives $v_p i=v_F$. Hence $v_F$ is a retract of the fibre trivial cofibration $i$ in $M_S$, and is a trivial cofibration by [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model]. Inverse reindexing along the bijection $f$ identifies its adjunct $u_F$ with the same map in $M_T$, using [lem-coef-enriched-fixed-set-model]. Thus $F$ is a total trivial cofibration. Step 8 supplies the reverse inclusion, identifying the second left lifting class.

source.place: Proposition 4.25, proof: both lifting systems, with the omitted dual argument supplied; Remark 5.5.

proof.text: Total fibrations are retract closed by their mappingwise description and the fibre retract axiom of [lem-coef-fixed-object-dg-free-model]. Total weak equivalences are retract closed as shown in step 5, so total trivial fibrations are too. If a map has the right lifting property against total cofibrations, its first factorization exhibits it as a retract of the trivial-fibration factor by [lem-coef-factorization-lifting-retracts]; hence it is a total trivial fibration. If it has the right lifting property against total trivial cofibrations, use the second factorization and the same right-retract clause of that node to make it a retract of a total fibration; hence it is a fibration. The reverse inclusions are the lifting assertions already proved. Both pairs are therefore weak factorization systems. Together with steps 5 and 6 this proves the total model axioms, with weak equivalences $\mathrm{FFB}$ and mappingwise projective fibrations.

source.place: Proposition 4.25, proof: both lifting systems, with the omitted dual argument supplied; Remark 5.5.

proof.text: The terminal total dg category has one object and zero mapping complex, with its unique unit and composition maps. Every complex maps surjectively to zero in each degree; by [lem-coef-projective-chains-monoidal-model] these maps are projective fibrations. The just-constructed mappingwise description therefore makes every dg category fibrant. Factor the initial map to $A$ by the first model factorization to choose a cofibrant replacement $q:QA\to A$ which is a trivial fibration. Its object function is a bijection by the description of $\mathrm{FFB}$.

source.place: Remark 5.5 and Example 5.11; model factorization of the initial map.

proof.text: Let $q_\infty:N\operatorname{Cat}(\mathbf V)\to\mathcal L$ be the infinity localization at $\mathrm{FFB}$ already identified, and let $L:\operatorname{Cat}(\mathbf V)\to h\mathcal L$ be its homotopy-category functor. This is an ordinary localization at $\mathrm{FFB}$: maps from an infinity-category to the nerve of an ordinary category factor uniquely through its homotopy category, since an ordinary target identifies homotopic arrows and has unique higher simplices over composable arrows. Applying the universal property of $q_\infty$ to such nerves gives precisely the ordinary localization universal property, with natural transformations. For $\alpha:LA\to LB$ and the chosen cofibrant replacement $q:QA\to A$, compose to obtain $\alpha L(q):L(QA)\to LB$. The source $QA$ is cofibrant and $B$ is fibrant by step 12. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective] to obtain an actual dg functor $t:QA\to B$ with $L(t)=\alpha L(q)$. Since $q$ is a weak equivalence, $\alpha=L(t)L(q)^{-1}$, which is the roof $A\xleftarrow{q}QA\xrightarrow{t}B$. This holds for the fixed chosen replacement of $A$. Finally the morphisms in $h\mathcal L$ are, by definition, the connected components of its mapping spaces, so every such component has the asserted roof representative.
